verses.text: At night on my bed, I looked for the one my soul loves. I looked for him, but I couldn't find him.
I'll get up now and go through the city. In the streets and squares I'll look for the one my soul loves. I looked for him, but I couldn't find him.
The watchmen making their rounds in the city found me. “Have you seen the one my soul loves?”
I'd barely passed them when I found the one my soul loves. I held him and wouldn't let him go until I'd brought him into my mother's house, into the room of the woman who conceived me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, swear to me by the gazelles and the deer of the field. Don't stir up or wake love until it wants to wake.
Who's this coming up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense and every kind of spice the merchant sells?
Look, it's Solomon's carriage! Sixty mighty men surround it, some of Israel's mightiest.
They're all skilled with the sword and experienced in war. Each has a sword at his thigh because of the dangers of the night.
King Solomon made himself a carriage out of wood from Lebanon.
He made its posts from silver, its base from gold, and its seat from purple cloth. The daughters of Jerusalem lined its inside with love.
Daughters of Zion, come out and see King Solomon in the crown his mother put on him on his wedding day, the day his heart rejoiced.
